findings.title: Spending limit budget addition is unchecked and can wrap
Ed25519 canonicalization is identity, so one key can be registered twice and satisfy an M-of-N threshold
Auth payload chooses the context rule, so a spending limit can be bypassed by routing a transfer through an unlimited rule for the same signer

findings.title: ExecutionEntryPoint::execute lets an authorized signer bypass policies and self-escalate via nested self-invocation
Transfer recipient not constrained by any policy
Soroban contract arithmetic can wrap around in release builds
Removing signers from a rule does not re-validate or notify the threshold policy, so the rule can become permanently unsatisfiable
set_threshold writes a threshold without checking the policy is installed for that rule, which blocks a later install
Failed policy uninstall is silently discarded while the rule and registry entry are removed
Weighted threshold feasibility check counts weights of signers outside the context rule
Threshold record is never TTL-extended on install or set, so a rarely used rule can lock after archival
Smart account instance storage and new rule entries never have their TTL extended
Weighted policy entry is read without TTL extension before the install check, so an archived entry blocks every authorization through the rule
Spending-limit history cap lets one authorized signer block a context rule for a full window
Public batch_add_signer helper mutates context-rule signers with no authorization check
